title: Popular tunes in Humphrey's lessons
summary: Humphrey would help students with popular music if they brought parts, and urged an instrument with more work.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, there's one thing I forgot to ask about Professor Humphrey's lessons. Did he ever let you work on any of the little popular tunes, any of those late numbers that came out? Did he ever give you anything like that? Well, yeah.
He always tried to advance your picture up.
I knew they wouldn't be in the Carl Fisher book. I wondered if you had some popular late songs and all too at that time.
Well, I think that if you could get somebody maybe would give you or lend you a part, you'd bring it there.
He would help you. He'd help you with any kind of music at all. I thought he might have stuck mostly to the marches and the Method book and not let you work on other kinds.

That's why he told me I was wasting my time fooling with a violin. He wanted me to get on an instrument that I could get out of. I played several jobs from Tronc Wonder with my father-in-law and others. I played Daphonis with him. This fellow here where I'm playing the bass horn, where I play the trombone with him. Oh, yeah. Yeah.
